events.title: The first Catholic diocese in the United States
events.shortBlurb: By the brief Ex hac apostolicae, Pope Pius VI made Baltimore the first see of the young republic and gave John Carroll to its scattered Catholics…
body: After the American Revolution the Catholics of the new United States had no bishop of their own. The clergy of Maryland and Pennsylvania, unwilling to remain a mere mission under the Congregation of Propaganda, petitioned Rome for a diocesan bishop, and Pope Pius VI took the unusual step of allowing them, for that first time only, to elect their candidate. Father John Carroll, a former Jesuit who had lived at Baltimore since 1786, was chosen by twenty-four of the twenty-six votes.

On 6 November 1789, by the pontifical brief Ex hac apostolicae, the pope erected the Diocese of Baltimore as the first in the United States, a see that then embraced the whole nation. Carroll was consecrated a bishop on 15 August 1790 in the chapel of Lulworth Castle in Dorset, England, by Charles Walmesley, vicar apostolic of the Western District.

Carroll had already helped found Georgetown in 1789; he held the first American diocesan synod in 1791, invited the English Dominicans, and established the Visitation nuns. In 1808 Pius VII raised Baltimore to a metropolitan archdiocese with the new suffragan sees of Bardstown, Boston, New York, and Philadelphia, so that the Church in the republic had its own hierarchy.
